tagline.text: A fishing-village beach and jump-off point for Santelmo and Taytayin coves in Nasugbu

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,500–3,800 (per person, costs shared by four)

children.text: Calayo Beach is a beach in a fishing village in Nasugbu, Batangas, and the starting point for boats to Santelmo, Taytayin and Kayraang coves. You can visit without advance booking, and it is a simple beach getaway about 3–4 hours from Manila.

Calayo Beach sits in Barangay Calayo in Nasugbu, Batangas. The village was a fishing community that has turned into a beach destination, and budget to mid-range resorts line the shore. The beach is not fine white sand; it has soft, light brown sand and calm water, so families with children visit often.

Much of the Nasugbu coast, including Punta Fuego, Pico de Loro and Hamilo Coast, Tali Beach and Canyon Cove, is open only to members or hotel guests. Calayo, by contrast, can be visited without advance booking, so it works well as a day trip or overnight from Manila. The biggest advantage is that boats to the neighboring coves leave from this village shore. If you drive, the faster route is said to be CAVITEX, then Antero Soriano Highway and Governor's Drive, and onto the Nasugbu–Ternate Highway. That road passes Mount Palay-Palay National Park and the Kaybiang Tunnel. By SLEX, take the Santa Rosa exit through Tagaytay, pass the Nasugbu welcome arch and town center, and turn onto the road to Calayo.

Island hopping usually runs from snorkeling at Santelmo Cove to cliff jumping at the Barracuda Cave in Taytayin Cove, and then the sandbar at Kayraang Cove. You can add camping beaches such as Layag-Layag Beach and Bituin Cove. Some coves are private property, so boats cannot dock and you enjoy them from just offshore. You hire one boat for the group, so the more people, the lower the cost per person. For Layag-Layag and Bituin, the package of boat plus water activities is about ₱3,000 for up to 6 people, and about ₱2,000 for the boat alone.

Calayo's main appeal is that it is simple to reach and not expensive. In return, many visitors report weak mobile signal in the village, and there are almost no public showers or toilets on the beach, so people usually buy a day-tour pass at a resort to wash up. Knowing this, you can enjoy a quiet fishing-village beach comfortably. One guide's budget example, with four people sharing costs, came to about ₱2,500 per person for a day trip and about ₱3,800 per person for an overnight stay. That covered the bus, tricycle, island hopping, resort day-use, lodging and meals.
The village shoreline is calm and quiet, good for walking on the sand and watching the sunset. Resorts and eateries along the shore make it easy to stay until evening.
It takes about
35 minutes

by boat from Calayo. The cove is private property, so you cannot land on the beach and instead snorkel a few meters offshore. One report mentions a seller of ice pops on the boat. Kayraang Cove and Bituin Cove now reportedly require advance booking even for day trips.
Near Taytayin Cove, cliff jumping from the high rock at Barracuda Cave is popular. Boats do not dock at the cove itself and stop at this spot.
It is
30–40 minutes
by boat from Taytayin. The cove is private property, so you cannot land; instead you step into the shallow water and enjoy a small sandbar.

Layag-Layag Beach in neighboring Papaya is famous for camping and requires a reservation. Guides cite an adult entrance fee of around ₱500 and an environmental fee of ₱30. The boat fare is separate, and reaching it by island-hopping boat reportedly means an extra charge to the boatman.
It is about
20 minutes
by boat from Calayo and is known as a camping spot. Guides cite about ₱300 per person for a day tour and about ₱500 for overnight, with a reservation required.
Village eateries and stores serve rice meals, side dishes and Batangas lomi. More variety is available in Nasugbu town.
Pulo Island (Loren Island), once part of island-hopping tours, is reportedly now closed to tourists. Check the current route locally.

items.title: 1 night 2 days
items.subtitle: Island hopping and the village beach

children.text: Take a bus to Nasugbu from Manila (Buendia or PITX).
Reach Calayo by tricycle from Nasugbu or Looc and drop your bags at your lodging.
Arrange a boat on the village shore and start island hopping in the order Santelmo, Taytayin and Kayraang.
Return to the village, wash up and watch the sunset.
Have dinner at a village eatery.
On day two, walk the beach in the morning, check out and head back to Manila in the afternoon.
Bus times and boat schedules are examples based on one guide. Actual times vary with traffic and weather.
Leave Manila for Nasugbu.
Arrive in Calayo, find a boat and start island hopping early.
Use a resort day-tour pass to shower and have lunch.
Head to the Nasugbu bus terminal and return to Manila.
A day trip is more relaxed if you leave early.
Take a DLTB bus from Buendia (corner of Gil Puyat Avenue and Taft Avenue) and get off at the Nasugbu bus terminal. The trip takes about
3–4 hours
, and a fare of about ₱240 has been reported.
From PITX there are buses to Nasugbu via the Kaybiang Tunnel, taking about
2–3 hours
for ₱220–230 or so. Get off at the basketball court across from the Looc barangay hall, and Calayo is close.
By car, take the Nasugbu–Ternate Highway from CAVITEX, or use SLEX and the Tagaytay–Nasugbu road.
From the Nasugbu bus terminal a tricycle takes about
30–45 minutes
, and guides cite ₱400–500 for two or three people.
From the Looc basketball court a tricycle takes about
10 minutes
and costs about ₱100 for up to three people.
The boat stations are Hulo, Centro and Sampaguita. A three-stop package is about ₱3,000 for up to 5 people, plus ₱500 for each extra person.
The island-hopping rate comes from a single recent source, so be sure to confirm it locally.
The dry season from November to May is best. January–March helps you avoid both rain and crowds, while March–May is summer holiday season and busy.
For a day trip, go early to enjoy the boats and the beach without rushing. A village ordinance reportedly allows swimming only from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

Around Nasugbu, May is busiest when school summer vacation overlaps, so weekdays from January to March suit anyone who wants a quiet beach. Island hopping can run long, so leave plenty of time before your bus back.

Calayo's shore has everything from budget lodging to mid-range resorts. A June 2026 guide says the long-running Calayo Beach Resort passed to new management and was renamed EMIKE Beach Resort, so check for the latest news before booking. Book early for weekends and holidays.

Around the village are small eateries and carinderias serving rice meals, side dishes and Batangas lomi. Nasugbu town has more variety, and places such as El Cocinero, with Spanish tapas and paella, and L'Bulalo, known for bulalo, are mentioned.

The Calayo Beach Resort described in one guide had a bamboo house for six with two bedrooms, a loft and a kitchen. Elsewhere in Nasugbu you will find large properties such as Pico Sands Hotel, Club Punta Fuego and Canyon Cove Hotel and Spa, and smaller ones such as RSAM Beach Resort, Shoreland Beach Resort, Seabreeze Beach Lodge and Sands Hotel Nasugbu. Parking is free at some resorts and costs about ₱50 by day and ₱100 overnight at others.
Facilities around the village are basic, so do not expect large supermarkets or amenities. Buy snacks, water and any medicine in advance at the Nasugbu town market or at roadside stores.
Many visitors report weak mobile signal in Calayo, so download offline maps and bring a power bank.
Put on your swimwear before boarding the boat so you can get in right at the first stop.
To protect marine life, use sunscreen without oxybenzone, benzophenone or parabens.
Ask the resort before pitching a tent. Some do not allow camping.
Paying the Nasugbu municipal environmental fee first and keeping the receipt is said to avoid being charged twice at other barangay checkpoints.
If you are not a strong swimmer, do not go far from shore. Agree on the itinerary and inclusions with your boatman beforehand.
Do not throw trash into the sea; carry it back to the mainland.
A checkpoint collects the environmental fee when you arrive in Calayo. Keep the receipt.
Nasugbu emergency contacts for the police, fire department, coast guard and Red Cross are published, so confirm and save them locally.
There are almost no public showers or toilets on Calayo's shore and the village sets swimming hours, so check resort use and the ordinance.
Santelmo and Kayraang coves are private property, so you cannot land, and some coves and camping beaches require advance booking.
Island-hopping rates and boat stations can change, so confirm with the boatman before you go.
Cliff jumping involves real height, so check the depth and safety and wear a life jacket.
In the rainy season high waves can keep boats from sailing, so check the weather.
In an emergency call the national emergency number 911, and save the numbers of Nasugbu police and the coast guard in advance.
With weak mobile signal, messages can be delayed, so confirm important bookings and boat arrangements ahead of time.
